FRANCHISE AGREEMENT

This Franchise Agreement (this "Agreement") is made as of October 12, 2026 by and between Copperleaf Kitchens Franchising, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company ("Franchisor"), and Meridian Hospitality Group LLC, an Arizona limited liability company ("Franchisee").

1. Grant of Franchise.

Franchisor grants Franchisee the right, and Franchisee accepts the obligation, to establish and operate one Copperleaf Kitchens restaurant (the "Franchised Business") at 1815 East Camelback Road, Phoenix, Arizona (the "Approved Location"), and to use the Marks and the System solely in connection with it. Franchisee acquires no right to operate at any other location or through any other channel.

2. Protected Territory.

Franchisor shall not establish, or license another party to establish, a Copperleaf Kitchens restaurant within a two (2) mile radius of the Approved Location during the term (the "Protected Territory"). The Protected Territory does not restrict Franchisor from selling Copperleaf-branded products through grocery, e-commerce, or any channel other than a restaurant, and does not grant Franchisee any right of first refusal for another location.

3. Term and Renewal.

The initial term is ten (10) years from the date the Franchised Business opens. Franchisee may renew for one additional term of ten (10) years if, not less than nine (9) and not more than twelve (12) months before the initial term expires, Franchisee gives written notice; is not in default; has remodeled the Franchised Business to Franchisor's then-current image standards; signs the then-current form of franchise agreement, which may differ materially from this Agreement; and signs a general release of claims against Franchisor, to the extent a release is enforceable under applicable law.

4. Fees.

4.1 Initial Franchise Fee. Franchisee shall pay an initial franchise fee of $45,000 on signing. The fee is fully earned when paid and is not refundable.

4.2 Royalty. Franchisee shall pay a royalty of six percent (6%) of Gross Sales, payable weekly by electronic funds transfer on Wednesday for the week ending the preceding Sunday. "Gross Sales" means all revenue from the Franchised Business, excluding sales tax collected and remitted and bona fide refunds.

4.3 Brand Fund. Franchisee shall contribute two percent (2%) of Gross Sales to the Copperleaf Brand Fund. Franchisor administers the Brand Fund, is not a fiduciary of it, and shall provide Franchisee an annual unaudited accounting of it on request. Franchisor is not obligated to spend the Brand Fund proportionately in Franchisee's territory.

4.4 Local Advertising. Franchisee shall spend not less than one percent (1%) of Gross Sales on local advertising in Franchisee's own market and shall submit materials to Franchisor for approval before use. Franchisor shall approve or deny within fifteen (15) days, and material not denied within that period is approved.

4.5 Late Payment. Any amount not paid when due bears interest at the lesser of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month and the maximum rate permitted by applicable law.

5. Training and Support.

Franchisor shall provide the initial training program described in the operations manual to Franchisee's principal and two managers at no additional tuition; on-site assistance for five (5) days at opening; the operations manual; and continuing guidance by telephone and email during business hours. Franchisee shall complete initial training to Franchisor's satisfaction before the Franchised Business opens.

6. Standards and the Operations Manual.

Franchisee shall operate the Franchised Business in strict compliance with the operations manual, as Franchisor may modify it from time to time, provided that no modification may materially increase Franchisee's obligations or costs beyond what is reasonable to protect the System. The operations manual is confidential, remains Franchisor's property, and shall be returned on termination. Franchisee shall purchase equipment, supplies, and food products meeting Franchisor's specifications, from suppliers Franchisor approves; Franchisor shall not unreasonably withhold approval of a supplier that meets its published specifications, and shall respond to a supplier request within thirty (30) days.

7. Marks.

Franchisee's use of the Marks inures solely to Franchisor's benefit. Franchisee acquires no ownership interest in the Marks, shall not register or attempt to register any mark confusingly similar to them, and shall use them only in the form and manner Franchisor prescribes. Franchisee shall notify Franchisor promptly of any infringement or challenge, and Franchisor has sole discretion whether to act. Franchisor shall indemnify Franchisee against a claim that Franchisee's authorized use of the Marks infringes another party's trademark rights, provided Franchisee gives prompt written notice, permits Franchisor to control the defense, and cooperates at Franchisor's expense.

8. Confidential Information.

Franchisee shall not, during or after the term, disclose or use for any purpose other than operating the Franchised Business any recipe, formula, method, supplier term, or other confidential information of the System. This obligation continues indefinitely as to a trade secret and for three (3) years after termination as to other confidential information.

9. Insurance.

Franchisee shall maintain commercial general liability insurance of not less than $2,000,000 per occurrence and $4,000,000 aggregate, liquor liability coverage if alcohol is served, workers' compensation as required by law, and property insurance on the Franchised Business, naming Franchisor as an additional insured, and shall furnish certificates annually.

10. Indemnification.

Franchisee shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Franchisor and its affiliates from all claims arising out of the operation of the Franchised Business, except to the extent caused by Franchisor's gross negligence or willful misconduct or covered by Franchisor's indemnity in Section 7. Franchisor shall give prompt written notice, may participate at its own expense, and shall not settle without Franchisee's consent where the settlement imposes an obligation on Franchisee.

11. Transfer.

Franchisee shall not transfer this Agreement, the Franchised Business, or a controlling interest in Franchisee without Franchisor's prior written consent, which Franchisor shall not unreasonably withhold if: the transferee meets Franchisor's then-current qualification standards; the transferee completes training; Franchisee pays a transfer fee of $10,000; all amounts owed are paid; and Franchisee signs a general release. Franchisor has a right of first refusal to purchase the Franchised Business on the same terms as a bona fide third-party offer, exercisable within thirty (30) days after Franchisee delivers the offer. Franchisor may assign this Agreement without Franchisee's consent to a party that assumes Franchisor's obligations.

12. Default and Termination.

12.1 Termination by Franchisor With Cure. Franchisor may terminate on thirty (30) days' written notice if Franchisee fails to pay any amount when due, fails to comply with a material standard, or otherwise materially breaches this Agreement, and does not cure within that period.

12.2 Termination by Franchisor Without Cure. Franchisor may terminate immediately on written notice if Franchisee: abandons the Franchised Business for five (5) consecutive days without Franchisor's consent; is convicted of a felony that materially and unfavorably affects the System; makes an unauthorized transfer; loses the right to occupy the Approved Location; or repeats the same material breach three times in twelve months after notice, whether or not each was cured.

12.3 Termination by Franchisee. Franchisee may terminate on sixty (60) days' written notice if Franchisor materially breaches this Agreement and does not cure within that period.

12.4 State Law. Where a state franchise-relationship law requires longer notice or a longer cure period than this Section provides, that law governs.

13. Post-Termination Obligations.

On expiration or termination Franchisee shall: immediately stop operating the Franchised Business and using the Marks and the System; deidentify the premises within thirty (30) days; return the operations manual and all confidential information; assign the telephone numbers, domain names, and social-media accounts used in the Franchised Business to Franchisor; and pay all amounts owed. Franchisor may, at its option, purchase the furniture, fixtures, equipment, and inventory of the Franchised Business at fair market value determined by an independent appraiser.

14. Covenant Not to Compete.

During the term and for twelve (12) months after termination or expiration, Franchisee and each owner of Franchisee shall not have any interest in a restaurant deriving more than twenty percent (20%) of its revenue from bowl-style prepared meals, located within five (5) miles of the Approved Location or of any Copperleaf Kitchens restaurant open at termination. This Section does not apply to an ownership interest of less than two percent (2%) in a publicly traded company, and applies only to the extent enforceable under applicable law.

15. Independent Contractor.

Franchisee is an independent contractor. Neither party is the agent, partner, joint venturer, or employee of the other. Franchisee is the sole employer of its employees, sets their wages and terms, and controls the day-to-day operation of the Franchised Business. Franchisee shall post a notice at the Franchised Business stating that it is independently owned and operated.

16. Dispute Resolution.

The parties shall first attempt to resolve any dispute by mediation in Maricopa County, Arizona, administered by the American Arbitration Association. A dispute not resolved within sixty (60) days after a written mediation request may be brought in the state or federal courts located in Maricopa County, Arizona, and each party consents to the jurisdiction of those courts. Nothing in this Section limits either party's right to seek injunctive relief. Where a state franchise law makes a forum outside the franchisee's state unenforceable, that law governs.

17. Acknowledgments.

Franchisee acknowledges that it received a Franchise Disclosure Document at least fourteen (14) calendar days before signing this Agreement or paying any consideration, that it has had the opportunity to consult counsel, and that no representation about actual or potential sales, income, or profits was made to it except as set out in Item 19 of the Franchise Disclosure Document. Nothing in this Section disclaims or waives any representation made in the Franchise Disclosure Document, and nothing here limits any right a franchisee has under a state franchise law or under the FTC Franchise Rule, 16 C.F.R. Part 436.

18. General.

This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Arizona, without regard to its conflict of laws principles, except that any state franchise-relationship law of the state in which the Franchised Business is located governs to the extent it applies. This Agreement, with its exhibits, is the entire agreement of the parties on its subject matter. It may be amended only by a writing signed by both parties. If any provision is unenforceable, the remainder remains in effect. It may be executed in counterparts.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have executed this Agreement as of the date first written above.
